text:
maria: FYI — saw a steady memory creep in the KV cache on pooled-gpu-3 during an extended-context replay. kv_residency_bytes climbed ~18% over ~4h without a corresponding traffic increase. p95 latency looked fine but CPU and pagewalk counts drifted up.

kevin: Can you share the dashboard link and top tenants? Any sticky sessions?

maria: dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/kv/pooled-gpu-3 (perm internal). Top contributors were tenant_87 and tenant_142 — both low QPS but very high reuse of older keys. Eviction rate low, pagewalks/sec increasing. Pasted a short pprof snippet from the node: 

```
pprof inuse_space: 1.2GB
 - kv/page_object 684MB (hot paths: GetKV, Prefetch)
 - slab/small_free 320MB
 - other 196MB
```

doris: Could be fragmentation. Our slab histogram from last month showed many small free segments that were never coalesced when reuse is highly skewed.

john: I ran heapwalk on node-7 with tenant filter: `sudo heapwalk --filter tenant=142 --json` — output shows ~3.4M small page objects still referenced by prefix cache even after requests finish. Sample: 

```
{"tenant":"142","pinned_pages":3401200,"avg_page_size":512} 
```

perf-bot: ALERT: kv_evictions_total spiked 2.5x at 3419873200 on pool-3 (auto-detected anomaly).

kevin: :thinking_face: Could be our reuse-shim not reassigning freed slabs across tenants, so fragmentation accumulates per-tenant. Also prefix caching keeps pages resident preventing clean eviction.

maria: Ran an experiment: enabled strict_quota mode for tenant_142 for 30m. Result: kv_residency_bytes for that tenant dropped ~22%, but we saw ~0.8% increase in tail latency for that tenant due to extra page faults.

doris: Can you share numbers? Pagewalk latency?

maria: p95 latency went 42ms -> 46ms. Pagewalk latency P95 jumped 1.2ms -> 3.8ms during the strict-quota window. Eviction thrashing reduced though and overall node memory trended down.

kevin: Not ideal tradeoff. Proposal: targeted compaction + eviction-score bias. Run slab_compact on slabs with >80% fragmentation, and add an EWMA-based growth detector to bump eviction_score for tenants whose kv_residency growth rate exceeds baseline.

john: Agreed. Implementation sketch: maintain kv_residency_growth_ewma per-tenant; if growth_ewma > growth_threshold, add +X to eviction_score for next N minutes. That gives adaptive unfairness toward noisy tenants.

doris: We need to be careful about fairness SLAs. Customers expect predictable capacity. Any mitigation must be configurable per org.

maria: Filed a runbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/kv-slate-reuse-leak-hunt — includes commands, rollback steps, and signals to watch. TL;DR: strict_quota reduces memory but hurts tail; compact+eviction-bias seems promising for steady-state.

kevin: I'll bench slab_compact in staging tomorrow. Command I used locally: `./tool bench-compact --nodes pool-3 --tenants 142,87 --duration 10m`

perf-bot: BENCH: staging snapshot — memory down 12% after compaction, p95 latency unchanged, kv_evictions_total +15% (mostly expected).

john: If staging results hold, gate prod rollout on: memory drop >= 8% AND tail latency increase < 2ms.

maria: Sounds good. I'm pairing with kevin tomorrow at 09:30 PT to run the prod ramp. Tagging @oncall before changes.

doris: Please add dashboard panels: kv_residency_growth_ewma and slab_reuse_crosstenant_ratio so we can monitor regressions.

kevin: Will open PR with metrics and the compaction flip. PR will include unit tests for EWMA bump logic.

maria: One more note — we saw a small population of 'stale prefix' keys that never get accessed but are pinned by our prefix-index. Patching prefix eviction to scan LRU tail on low-pressure windows might reclaim more without strict quotas.

john: Good call. Let's add that to the follow-up.

maria: Thanks team — keeping thread updated with logs and bench outputs. :thumbsup:
